findings.explanation: The producer domain names input was validated only for a trailing dot, so a list of two or more domains passed validation and plan; the provider documents 'Current max number of domain names supported is 1' but does not enforce it in schema, so the API rejects it at apply. Principle is a best fit: this is an apply-time correctness bug.
findings.remediation: Validate that at most one domain is given.
findings.title: Service attachment domain_names accepts several domains but GCP supports only one

findings.explanation: Both addresses are created with count driven by whether var.consumer / var.google_apis is set, and both carry a hard-coded lifecycle.prevent_destroy. Setting either input back to null, changing var.name (ForceNew on the address name), or removing the module call fails plan with 'Instance cannot be destroyed', and a caller of the published module cannot override lifecycle, so the only way out is state surgery. The Google APIs address is always pinned to var.google_apis.ip_address, so a replacement would keep its IP anyway; only an auto-allocated consumer IP is at risk.
findings.remediation: Decide whether IP stability or the optional-part interface wins: drop prevent_destroy (and recommend pinning consumer.ip_address), or keep it and document that the parts are one-way once created.
findings.title: prevent_destroy on count-toggled PSC addresses makes the consumer and Google APIs parts impossible to disable or rename

findings.explanation: The provider expands google_compute_subnetwork.ip_cidr_range in place only when the new range contains the old one; any other change to var.producer.nat_cidr forces replacement. Terraform's default destroy-then-create deletes the NAT subnet before updating google_compute_service_attachment.producer.nat_subnets, and GCP refuses to delete a PSC NAT subnet a service attachment still uses (resourceInUseByAnotherResource), so the apply fails half-way. Adding create_before_destroy alone would not help: the subnet name "${var.name}-psc-nat" is static and the new subnet would collide with it. Principle is a best fit: this is an apply-time correctness bug.
findings.remediation: Either make the NAT subnet name unique per range (for example suffix it with a short hash of nat_cidr) and add lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }, so the new subnet is attached before the old one is removed, or document in var.producer that nat_cidr can only be widened in place and any other change needs the producer part removed and recreated.
findings.title: Changing producer.nat_cidr to a non-superset range fails apply: the NAT subnet is destroyed while the service attachment still uses it

suggested_policies.rationale: holden has no policy for google_compute_service_attachment. With connection_preference = ACCEPT_AUTOMATIC any project that knows the attachment URI can create a PSC endpoint into the producer's internal load balancer; ACCEPT_MANUAL restricts connections to consumer_accept_lists. The check is one attribute with a fixed value and applies to any Terraform using the resource. This module already hard-codes ACCEPT_MANUAL, so it passes.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Private Service Connect service attachments must require manual consumer acceptance
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A service attachment with connection_preference ACCEPT_AUTOMATIC accepts a
  PSC endpoint from any project that knows its URI, exposing the published
  internal load balancer to arbitrary consumers. ACCEPT_MANUAL limits
  connections to the projects and networks in consumer_accept_lists.
message: |
  google_compute_service_attachment does not set connection_preference to ACCEPT_MANUAL.
remediation: |
  Set connection_preference = "ACCEPT_MANUAL" and list the allowed consumers:
    consumer_accept_lists {
      project_id_or_num = "consumer-project"
      connection_limit  = 10
    }
resources:
  google_compute_service_attachment:
    path: connection_preference
    equals: ACCEPT_MANUAL
